report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to produce keyword-style, section‑header/label outputs (i.e., noun‑heavy, title‑cased tags) — effectively a keyword/topic extractor or structured summary formatter rather than a natural prose continuer.

Reasoning:
- Location of signal: The difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across layers, consistent with a global “output style” shift that kicks in right at generation start (typical of instruction/format finetunes).
- Vocabulary direction (logit lens): Across layers and positions 1–4, the top tokens are dominated by title‑cased, noun/label words and proper nouns rather than function words or verbs: “Summary”, “Outcome”, “File”, “Computation”, “Students”, “Amounts”, “Maximum”, “Weight”, “MPEG”, “HDTV”, “Playboy”, “TMZ”, “DJI”, “Waiter”, plus domain nouns like “asbestos”, “hydrocarbon”, “landfill”, “luciferase”. These look like tags/headers/categories more than sentence continuations.
- Consistency across positions: The same small set of section‑like labels (“Summary”, “Outcome”, “File”, “Computation”) repeatedly tops positions 1–4 in many mid/late layers, matching the behavior of producing multi‑item keyword lists or structured sections rather than free text.
- Morphology/lemmatization flavor: Stems like “astrolog” and “iasis” appear, consistent with emitting lemma‑like keyword forms. There is a notable absence of ordinary connectors/punctuation that would signal sentence generation.

Taken together, the B–A difference points to Model B being trained to output structured, capitalized labels/keywords (topic/entity tags or section headers), i.e., a keyword/section summarizer, rather than to change factual knowledge or general next‑token predictions.
